setupGuide.title: Setup guide
setupGuide.summary: Recommended DCS setup and compatible titles
setupGuide.heading: Recommended DCS setup
setupGuide.game: {label} turn on {useQuadView} and, for gaze tracking, {useEyeTracking}.
setupGuide.provider: {label} enable the VectorXR layer and Quadviews profile, then disable {layerName}. On Pimax, also turn Native Pimax Quad Views off. Native Varjo Quadviews remains runtime-driven.
setupGuide.apply: {label} save the profile and restart DCS after changing runtime, layer, or in-game VR settings.
setupGuide.titles: DCS is the primary tested title. Likely, but unconfirmed, D3D11 candidates include Pavlov VR, VAIL VR, The 7th Guest VR, and Kayak VR: Mirage. Each title must request quad views itself.
setupGuide.pixelEstimates: Pixel estimates compare application view rendering only; the runtime and VectorXR composite have additional GPU cost.

varjo.title: Varjo Compatible Quadviews
varjo.biPanel: Varjo headsets are bi-panel: a wide, lower-density context display plus a small, high-density focus display per eye. VectorXR's Varjo compatible quadviews keeps the four view layers your headset expects (two peripheral, two focus) so the physical focus panels are driven directly. As a consequence, the Varjo runtime takes over the view geometry, and some Quadviews settings are ignored.
varjo.notesIntro: VectorXR Quadviews & Varjo runtime compatibility notes:
varjo.emulation: On headsets without physical quad-view support through bi-panel displays (e.g. Quest Pro, Pimax Crystal), VectorXR Quadviews uses the standard emulation mode and all settings apply. These compatibility notes apply only to Varjo runtimes.
varjo.diagnosticUnsupportedLead: Diagnostic visualization is not currently supported on Varjo headsets.
varjo.diagnosticUnsupported: {lead} Varjo's runtime owns the native quad-view composition, so VectorXR's synthesized D3D11 compositor does not run there.

preset.heading: Vector Preset
preset.restartTitle: Presets include settings that require a game restart for their complete effect.
preset.intro: A strong starting point; tracking and alignment remain yours.
preset.buttonTitle: Presets change focus dimensions and resolution, so their complete effect requires a game restart.

focusWidth.label: Focus Width
focusWidth.restart: The focus window moves live, but DCS keeps its existing texture width and pixel workload until restart.

focusHeight.label: Focus Height
focusHeight.restart: The focus window moves live, but DCS keeps its existing texture height and pixel workload until restart.

horizontalOffset.label: Horizontal Offset
horizontalOffset.help: Moves the focus area left or right in degrees. Use this only if the sharp region feels off-center.

verticalOffset.label: Vertical Offset
verticalOffset.help: Moves the focus area up or down in degrees. Helpful if a headset's gaze center feels vertically biased.

focusResolution.label: Focus Resolution
focusResolution.restart: Restart required: DCS keeps its launch-time focus textures. Above 100% can resize VectorXR's output canvas and may cause a temporary frame-rate hitch.
focusResolution.warning: VectorXR's full-view output image grows with Focus Resolution: {percent}% needs about {factor}× your headset's pixels in GPU memory and compositing, on top of the app render cost shown above.

peripheralResolution.label: Peripheral Resolution
peripheralResolution.restart: Restart required: DCS keeps its launch-time peripheral textures and pixel workload.

foveateSharpness.label: Foveate Sharpness
foveateSharpness.help: Applies extra sharpening to the high-detail focus image. 0 is off; higher values add crispness but can create halos.

transitionThickness.label: Transition Thickness
transitionThickness.help: Controls how wide the blended edge is between the focus and peripheral images. Higher values hide the boundary better but soften more of the focus window.

mode.label: Mode
mode.restart: Switching to Eye tracked needs a game restart when the game started in Head tracked mode.
mode.help: Chooses whether the focus area follows head direction or eye gaze when eye tracking is available.
mode.head: Head tracked

eyeTrackingCorrection.label: Eye Tracking Correction
eyeTrackingCorrection.help: Use Default unless eye tracking feels backwards; then try Flip Z Only.

smoothing.label: Smoothing
smoothing.help: Softens focus-area movement. 0 is instant; higher values reduce jitter but add lag.

deadzone.label: Deadzone
deadzone.help: Small gaze movements ignored before the focus area moves. Useful for reducing shimmer near center.

dimensions.waiting: View dimensions appear here while a Quadviews game is running.
dimensions.footer: Submitted view sizes, refreshed every second. Saved resolution changes may require a game restart.

troubleshoot.summary: Map a symptom to the right control.

guide.illustrationLabel: Interactive illustration of the Quadviews diagnostic overlay

svg.dragHint: CLICK OR DRAG TO MOVE RAW GAZE

guide.illustrative: Illustrative - not a pixel-perfect headset capture

peripheral.title: Peripheral area
peripheral.body: Blue covers the context image. Lowering its resolution usually saves the most pixels without shrinking your sharp region.

transition.title: Transition band
transition.body: Amber is the blend between images. Wider can hide a seam; too wide can make the edge feel soft.

focusBoundary.title: Focus boundary
focusBoundary.body: The green outline is the focus window size. Focus Resolution changes detail density, not this outline.

headCenter.title: Head center
headCenter.body: The white cross is straight ahead from the headset. It gives every other marker a stable reference.

configuredOffset.title: Configured offset
configuredOffset.body: The magenta L and ring show your intentional correction from head center.

rawGaze.title: Raw gaze
rawGaze.body: Cyan is the immediate eye-tracking sample. Click the illustration to move it.

smoothedGaze.title: Smoothed gaze
smoothedGaze.body: Yellow is the filtered position that drives the focus window before configured offset is added.

greenOutline.title: Green outline
greenOutline.body: Eye tracking is available. Compare cyan and yellow to judge filtering.

redOutline.title: Red outline
redOutline.body: The eye source is unavailable. VectorXR is using its fallback focus behavior.

goodTracking.heading: What good tracking looks like
goodTracking.cyan: Cyan responds immediately to your eyes.
goodTracking.yellow: Yellow follows closely without constant trembling.
goodTracking.window: The focus window stays on the intended detail.

boundary.label: Visible seam
boundary.title: The focus edge is easy to see
boundary.body: Increase Transition Thickness a little. If the amber band becomes broadly soft, reduce it again and narrow the resolution difference between Focus and Peripheral.

offset.label: Wrong center
offset.title: The sharp region is consistently biased
offset.body: First confirm the cyan and yellow gaze markers land where you look. If they do, use Horizontal or Vertical Offset to correct the consistent bias. Do not use offset to hide gaze lag.

jitter.label: Jitter
jitter.title: The focus window trembles near your gaze
jitter.body: Raise Smoothing gradually. A small Deadzone can suppress tiny eye movements near center, but too much creates a sticky jump when the focus finally moves.

lag.label: Too much lag
lag.title: The yellow marker trails too far behind cyan
lag.body: Reduce Smoothing. If movement starts late and then jumps, reduce Deadzone too. Use the smallest values that still keep the focus window visually calm.

lost.label: Red outline
lost.title: Eye tracking is unavailable
lost.body: A red focus outline is a status warning, not a color preference. Confirm eye tracking is enabled in the game and headset runtime. VectorXR falls back instead of following eye gaze.

performance.label: Need more FPS
performance.title: Reduce pixels where they matter least
performance.body: Lower Peripheral Resolution first. Then reduce Focus Width or Height if needed. Focus Resolution changes density inside the window - it does not change the green outline size.

tuningOrder.heading: Good tuning order:
tuningOrder.quality: Then tune image quality and pixel cost.
